definitions.gloss: highest-ranking courtesan; oiran of the top rank
definitions.explanation: The most elite rank of courtesan in Edo-period pleasure quarters, distinguished by exceptional beauty, cultural refinement, and artistic accomplishments.

definitions.gloss: lead performer; master narrator or puppeteer
definitions.explanation: A title for high-ranking performers in traditional Japanese arts, especially the lead chanter in bunraku puppet theater and certain Noh performers.

examples.japanese: {太夫|たゆう}は{教養|きょうよう}と{美貌|びぼう}を{兼|か}ね{備|そな}えていた。
examples.english: The tayuu combined refinement and beauty.

examples.japanese: {吉原|よしわら}の{太夫|たゆう}は{最高位|さいこうい}の{遊女|ゆうじょ}として{特別|とくべつ}な{待遇|たいぐう}を{受|う}けた。
examples.english: Tayuu of Yoshiwara received special treatment as the highest-ranking courtesans.

examples.japanese: {太夫|たゆう}になるには{和歌|わか}や{茶道|さどう}、{書道|しょどう}など{多|おお}くの{芸事|げいごと}に{通|つう}じていなければならなかった。
examples.english: To become a tayuu, one had to be well-versed in many arts including waka poetry, tea ceremony, and calligraphy.

examples.japanese: {文楽|ぶんらく}の{太夫|たゆう}が{語|かた}り{始|はじ}めた。
examples.english: The bunraku narrator began to chant.

examples.japanese: {人間国宝|にんげんこくほう}の{太夫|たゆう}の{語|かた}りは{圧巻|あっかん}だった。
examples.english: The performance of the narrator designated as a Living National Treasure was magnificent.

examples.japanese: {文楽|ぶんらく}では{太夫|たゆう}が{物語|ものがたり}を{語|かた}り、{三味線|しゃみせん}{弾|ひ}きが{伴奏|ばんそう}し、{人形遣|にんぎょうつか}いが{人形|にんぎょう}を{操|あやつ}る{三位一体|さんみいったい}の{芸能|げいのう}である。
examples.english: Bunraku is a performing art in which the tayuu narrates the story, the shamisen player accompanies, and the puppeteers manipulate the puppets — a trinity of arts.

notes:
An important term in Japanese cultural history with two distinct but related meanings. Both senses share the idea of being at the top of a hierarchy.

Also written as {大夫|たゆう}. The alternate reading だゆう exists but たゆう is standard.

ETYMOLOGY:
The courtesan sense dates to the Edo period (1603-1868). {太夫|たゆう} were the elite of the pleasure quarters, particularly {吉原|よしわら} in Edo and {島原|しまばら} in Kyoto. Unlike lower-ranking courtesans, they could refuse clients and were celebrated for their cultural accomplishments. The {太夫|たゆう} rank gradually disappeared by the mid-Edo period as the {花魁|おいらん} system replaced it.

The performer sense remains alive in {文楽|ぶんらく} (bunraku puppet theater), where the {太夫|たゆう} is the chanter who narrates the entire story.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {花魁|おいらん}: oiran — high-ranking courtesans who succeeded the {太夫|たゆう} system
- {遊女|ゆうじょ}: courtesan; prostitute — the general term for women in the pleasure quarters
- {語|かた}り{手|て}: narrator — a general term for a storyteller in any context
